::: {#thm-cartesian-cancel}
#### Cancelling a factor of a Cartesian product

Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets with $C \ne \emptyset$.
If $A \times C = B \times C$, then $A = B$ (@def-cartesian-product).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Suppose $A \times C = B \times C$.
Since $C \ne \emptyset$, there is some $c \in C$ (@def-empty-set).

($\subseteq$)
Let $a \in A$.
Then $(a, c) \in A \times C$.
Since $A \times C = B \times C$, also $(a, c) \in B \times C$,
so $(a, c) = (b, c')$ for some $b \in B$ and $c' \in C$ (@def-cartesian-product).
Two ordered pairs are equal only when their first entries are equal (@def-ordered-pair),
so $a = b$, and $a \in B$.

($\supseteq$)
Let $b \in B$.
Then $(b, c) \in B \times C = A \times C$,
so $b \in A$, by the same steps with $A$ and $B$ swapped.

So $A = B$ (@thm-double-inclusion).

:::

:::
